newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo rubber prices rise as rain hits supply.
newsitem.headline: Colombo rubber prices rise as rain hits supply.

text.p: Rubber prices rose at the Colombo auction on Thursday as exporters scrambled for the 56 tonnes of crepe and seven tonnes of sheet, brokers said.
"Rain has brought quantities down to very low levels," said Shehan Meegama of brokers John Keells. "This is likely to be the case in the coming weeks too."
The average offer at the auction is 200 to 300 tonnes.

For the past month, inter-monsoon showers have been lashing the country, bringing rubber tapping to a virtual standstill. The country's northeast monsoon normally begins in mid-November after the May-June southwest monsoon.
Exporters said aggressive buying of the small quantity available pushed prices up.
"Buyers have been waiting for larger quantities to come into the market," a leading exporter said. "Today, they ran out of patience, entered the market and began buying."
Best latex one-x, the purest grade, was 75 rupees per kilo, up 1.45 rupees from the last auction on Tuesday. Number one was 73.50 rupees, up from 72. RSS1 fetched 65 rupees, up 10 cents.
